note.backdrop: The morning's rally reversed into a market-wide fall. At 12:37 ET the S&P 500 fund was -1.5%, the Nasdaq 100 fund -1.6%, small companies -2.1% and the VIX +8.1%, against +1.3%, +2.2% and +0.7% before the open: a swing of about 2.8 points in the S&P 500 fund. The check flagged a market-wide move. Yahoo Finance's live page: losses accelerated as Anthropic opened 34% above its offer price ($111.50 against $83); AMD fell as much as 9% after a short seller opened a position citing its China ties; the rotation out of healthcare continued, UnitedHealth on track for an 18% fall over five days; tech was briefly the only sector up before it too fell. Oil, the dollar and yields are flat; gold -1.4%. 8 stocks are outside their 9-in-10 range and 63 outside their 2-in-3 range, from 2 and 7 this morning.

read.says: Dow -2% (over 1,000 points), S&P 500 -1.5%, Nasdaq -1.5% as Anthropic opened at $111.50, 34.3% above its $83 IPO price; AMD fell as much as 9% after Hunterbrook Capital opened a short position citing its China ties; UnitedHealth -5%, on track for an 18% fall over five days; Amazon -0.9% and Alphabet +0.7% after the first trade; retail got about 15% of the offering.

Anthropic began trading at $111.50 on Nasdaq as ANT; 980 million shares at $83 for about $81.3 billion plus a $26 billion private placement; as many as 315 million shares held by non-founder executives, directors, employees and consultants could become eligible for sale on the first day, generally up to 10% of their locked-up holdings.

StoneX's fourth quarter: diluted EPS $0.66 against a $0.81 consensus; net operating revenues $655.2 million (+12%); net income $84.2 million (-2%); shares -6.2% after hours Wednesday; fiscal-year net income a record $525.4 million.
Insmed rose about 18% after Bloomberg reported that Sanofi is speaking with advisers about a potential acquisition; any deal could be weeks away and neither company has confirmed talks.

Valvoline's fiscal 2026: sales $2.1 billion (+21%), system-wide same-store sales +7.9%, adjusted EBITDA $557 million (+19%), adjusted EPS $1.76 (+11%); it expects another year of strong growth in fiscal 2027.

singles.beneath: In proportion: a 19% EPS miss in one quarter of a record year ($525.4 million of net income, +72%) does not by itself explain a fall from -6% after hours to -26% in session; about $1.8 billion of value on a $6.7 billion company. Something beyond the reported miss, or forced selling on a market-wide down day, is likely; the cause of the size is not established.
singles.cause: StoneX is -26.3% after its fourth quarter: EPS $0.66 against a $0.81 consensus, net income -2% (Investing.com). It fell 6.2% after hours on the report.

singles.beneath: A report of deliberations, not an offer: Insmed was worth about $26.3 billion before the move, so the jump adds about $5 billion on the chance of a deal. If no deal follows, the move is the market's estimate of that chance times a premium, which it will give back.
singles.cause: Insmed is +19.6% after Bloomberg reported that Sanofi is weighing an acquisition; neither company has confirmed talks (Proactive; Tikr; Stocktwits).

themes.beneath: In proportion: at $111.50 Anthropic was valued above SpaceX at its listing; its fall to about $99.75 is 10.5% from the first trade. Fox Business reports that up to 315 million shares held by employees and others could be sold from the first day, so supply arrived with the debut. For the desk's calls (judged at Friday's close against Nov 13's): Nvidia at $149.88 is 7.99% below $162.89, past its 7.5% line; AMD at $489.85 is 8.07% below $532.84, short of its 9% line ($484.88); Dell at $320.61 is 6.50% below $342.98, short of its 9.5% line. Nothing is decided until Friday's close.
themes.cause: Anthropic opened at $111.50, 34% above its $83 offer price, and has since slid to about $99.75, still 20% above it (Fox Business; Yahoo Finance). The morning's AI gains are gone: CoreWeave -4.1%, IREN -3.0%, Vertiv -2.8%, Applied Digital -2.0%, Broadcom -1.6%, Marvell -1.4%, Nvidia -0.6%; Amazon -2.0%. AMD -9.5% has its own reported cause: a short seller's report on its China ties (Yahoo Finance; I could not read the report itself). Intel +3.8% still holds its own news.
themes.mechanism: The rally of the morning was bought on the expectation of a strong debut; once the debut happened, there was nothing left to wait for, and holders sold (profit-taking is how the sources describe it). Money that bought Anthropic at the open had to come from somewhere, and the obvious source is other AI holdings; that is my inference, untested.

themes.watch: Where Anthropic closes against $83 and $111.50; whether the AI group closes at today's lows. A close back above this morning's levels would say the selling was only the first-trade rush.

themes.beneath: Four days of falls with no new information. The group's selling now lines up with the market's (small companies -2.1%, the VIX up 8%), so part of today's fall is the market, not the rule.

themes.mechanism: No new reported news beyond the Medicare Advantage audit proposal of Nov 16. Today Cigna, which held up best on Tuesday and Wednesday, fell most, and Humana, which fell most, fell least: the selling is spreading to the companies the proposal touches less. That reading is mine.

themes.mechanism: These companies sell people's time for work that AI models are sold to do. On the day the largest AI model maker listed at about $1.5 trillion, the market marked down the companies its product is said to replace. That is my inference only; the same companies also fall with the market and with weak job data.
